Consistency of OLS (Not Tested)   Law of large numbers(LLN)

Definition





Weak Law of Large Numbers

Suppose X1, X2, · · · , Xn is a sequence of i.i.d. random variables with an expected
value µ < ∞and a variance σ2 < ∞, Xn converges in probability to µ, that is,
for any ϵ > 0, we have:

                  n→∞P(|Xnlim      −µ| < ϵ) →1
Denoted as ”plim(Xn) = µ” or ”Xn p−→µ”.

Consistency of OLS (Not Tested)    Consistency

Definition





Consistency

An estimator ˆθn (based on a sample of n size) is consistent for a population
parameter θ if for any ϵ > 0:

                       n→∞P(|ˆθnlim     −θ| < ϵ) →1
                                          or

                                  plim(ˆθn) = θ

Consistency of OLS (Not Tested)    Consistency of OLS

Consistency of OLS estimator



Theorem 5.1 Consistency of OLS

Under MLR.1-MLR.4, OLS estimators ˆβj is consistent for βj for all
j = 0, 1, 2, · · · , k

                         plim(ˆβj) = βj, j = 0, 1, 2, · · · , k



Comments:
     Consistency is a minimal requirement for an estimator.

    OLS estimator is consistent under the weaker assumption MLR.4’:
    E(u) = 0, Cov(xj, u) = 0.
     Note: unbiasedness ⇎consistency

Comments

       If the sample size is large enough, t-, F-tests as well as confidence intervals
     are still valid without holding MLR.6.

Dummy Variable    Single dummy variable

Single dummy variable


Definition:

   A Dummy variable (indicator variable) is one that takes a binary value
    (0 or 1), which is typically used to encode categorical features.


Qualitative information described,e.g.:

    Gender (male or female)                Region (domestic or foreign)

    Nationality (majority or minority)        Type (SOE or POE)

Interpretation of the ˆβ1,e.g.:

     \                       log(wage) = ˆβ0 + ˆβ1female


    The average wage of a female is higher (or lower) than that of a male by
     |100ˆβ1%|, holding the other factors fixed.

Dummy Variable    Multiple dummy variables

Multiple dummy variables





Using dummy variables for multiple categories:

     Define membership in each category by a dummy variable.

     Leave out one category(which becomes the base category), to avoid the
   dummy variable trap.


Dummy variable trap:

    The problem occurs when we create k dummy variables instead of k-1
   dummy variables to describe k groups.

     Perfect colinearity exists in this case.

Dummy Variable    Linear probability model

Linear probability model




Definition:

    The multiple linear regression model with a binary dependent variable:

                 E(y|x) = P(y = 1|x) = β0 + β1x1 + · · · + βkxk



Drawbacks:

     Predicted probability may < 0 or > 1, which makes no sense in practice.

     Estimated partial effects could only be constant.

    Must have heteroskedasticity (y is a Bernoulli distribution rather than normal;
    V ar(u) is a function of x)

Stata Commands for Probability Models

Syntax



When y is a binary variable, we can use Stata to estimate the following models:

1)linear probability model:

                                  reg y x1 x2 x3



2)probit model:

                                  probit y x1 x2 x3



3)logit model:

                                      logit y x1 x2 x3
